newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby league-Manly outclass St George for ARL title.
newsitem.headline: Rugby league-Manly outclass St George for ARL title.

text.p: Manly outclassed St George on Sunday to win the Australian Rugby League (ARL) grand final 20-8 and lift their first premiership trophy in nine years.

Australia coach Bob Fulton's Manly side topped the ARL regular season standings and built their grand final win on an almost impregnable defensive line which St George was only able to breach for the first time late in the match.
Manly scored three tries to St George's one in front of 40,983 fans at the Sydney Football Stadium and led 14-2 at halftime.

Controversy surrounded Manly's second try by second-rower Steve Menzies after referee David Manson allowed New Zealand fullback Matthew Ridge to play on after being apparently tackled by St George hooker Nathan Brown.
Menzies scored from the next ruck and St George players argued with Manson as they left the field at halftime.

Manly's first try came after just five minutes when centre Craig Innes grounded a short kick by captain Geoff Toovey. Winger Danny Moore put the match beyond doubt when he scored his side's third try after a St George error 13 minutes into the second half.
Winger Nick Zisti crossed for St George 20 minutes from fulltime as his side played increasingly desperate football.
"We had a tough game on our hands and it's even better to win when they are the circumstances," Fulton told reporters.

St George had been rated 100-1 outsiders at the start of the year after losing two coaches and several key players during the ARL's battle for control of the game with media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's banned breakaway Super League.
The 75-year-old club also narrowly avoided a merger with Sydney City at the start of the year over financial problems caused by the Super League war.

St George finished seventh at the end of regular season matches but compiled a list of stirring victories during the play-off series, beating higher-ranked sides Canberra, Sydney City and North Sydney to reach the grand final.
"We didn't save our best game till last, unfortunately," St George coach David Waite told reporters.
The grand final was the last match for former Australia players David Gillespie and Des Hasler, who had announced they would retire at the end of this season.
Hasler played in Manly's previous premiership winning side in 1987 and in the side beaten by Sydney Bulldogs in last year's grand final.
